exposure: Intraplacental injections of non-viral polymeric nanoparticles containing a human insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF1) transgene
Intraplacental injections of nanoparticles containing a GFP-expressing plasmid
outcome: Placental uptake and transient transgene expression
cohort: Pregnant macaques were studied after ultrasound-guided intraplacental injections of nanoparticles.
finding: IGF1 nanoparticle treatment resulted in no adverse maternal reaction, with maternal blood parameters remaining normal and placental signaling adapting to maintain homeostasis, indicating no deleterious impact during the acute study phase.
